scope: Curated source-verified diagnostic families; lexical inventory is broader than structured parser support.
runtime_status_policy: source_only means this catalog entry documents source behavior. Runtime evidence is separately recorded in the crash corpus manifest; neither catalog inclusion nor source candidates claim runtime or parser coverage.

families.title: Assertion / panic
families.description: File, line, task, assertion PC and execution context.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("Assertion failed at file:%s line: %d task: %s\n", filename, lineno, fault_tcb->name);
lldbg("Assertion failed at file:%s line: %d task: %s\n", filename, lineno, fault_tcb->name);
lldbg_noarg("Assertion failed CPU%d at file: %s line %d", cpu, filename, lineno);
lldbg("Assertion failed at file:%s line: %d task: %s\n", filename, lineno, fault_tcb->name);

analysis_guidance: Preserve the earliest failure and the file/line/task together. A fault-handler PANIC assertion is downstream of the preceding fault, not automatically the originating defect.
Map addresses only with the exact image and binary load map.
limitations: Serial prefixes and file names can be truncated; absence of a complete assertion is not absence of a crash.

families.title: Cortex-M HardFault
families.description: Escalated/configurable fault details and saved registers.
analysis_guidance: CFAULTS is the firmware label for CFSR; HFAULTS is HFSR. Decode architecture-specific bits and preserve raw words.
A forced HardFault requires the underlying CFSR evidence. Do not interpret every BFAULTADDR value as valid.
limitations: Fault output may be suppressed by debug routing, or fail during a nested fault.

families.title: Cortex-M MPU / memory-management fault
families.description: Instruction/data access violation, stacking failure, MMFAR.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("PANIC!!! Memory Management Fault at instruction : 0x%08x\n", regs[REG_R15]);
lldbg("PANIC!!! Memory Management Fault at instruction : 0x%08x\n", regs[REG_R15]);

analysis_guidance: Check MMARVALID before treating MMFAR as faulting address.
Distinguish MPU XN instruction access from data RW permissions and exception stacking failures.
limitations: An MPU violation alone does not establish a physical flash-bus/XIP stall.

families.title: Cortex-M BusFault
families.description: Precise/imprecise bus fault, BFAR, exception entry/return faults.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("PANIC!!! Bus fault at instruction: 0x%08x\n", regs[REG_R15]);
lldbg("PANIC!!! Bus fault at instruction: 0x%08x\n", regs[REG_R15]);

analysis_guidance: Require BFARVALID for a trusted BFAR.
For IMPRECISERR the saved PC can be later than the initiating store; investigate bus/peripheral accesses before the exception.
limitations: QEMU bus responses do not reproduce every board peripheral or physical timing failure.

families.title: Cortex-M UsageFault
families.description: Undefined instruction, invalid state/return, coprocessor, alignment, divide-by-zero and v8-M STKOF.
analysis_guidance: Use architecture/config to interpret status bits; STKOF is v8-M-specific in this source.
Correlate invalid state/return with xPSR, EXC_RETURN, stack frame and exact disassembly.
limitations: The handler prints a priority-ordered fault-type branch; raw CFSR may contain multiple bits.

families.title: ARMv7-A/R aborts
families.description: Data/prefetch abort and undefined-instruction state distinct from Cortex-M fault registers.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("\nData abort. PC: %08x DFAR: %08x DFSR: %08x\n", regs[REG_PC], dfar, dfsr);
lldbg("\nPrefetch abort. PC: %08x IFAR: %08x IFSR: %08x\n", regs[REG_PC], ifar, ifsr);

analysis_guidance: Decode DFSR/IFSR using the appropriate A/R architecture; never apply Cortex-M CFSR masks to them.
Keep PC, DFAR/IFAR and status together and account for MMU mappings.
limitations: No QEMU ARMv8-M execution can validate ARMv7-A/R handlers.

families.title: Saved CPU registers
families.description: R0/R8 groups, status/control registers and banked A/R registers.
analysis_guidance: Associate register sets with each crash/context instead of merging repeated keys across reboots.
Respect split print calls on A-profile: one physical line can be assembled by several emitters.
limitations: Task snapshots and live handler registers are different contexts; annotate saved/current labels.

families.title: Stack region and raw words
families.description: Task/IRQ/nested-IRQ bounds, usage, invalid SP and hexadecimal memory rows.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("Current SP is User Thread SP: %08x\n", sp);
lldbg("ERROR: Stack pointer is not within any of the allocated stack\n");

analysis_guidance: Compare SP to the correct active stack region and architecture growth direction.
Memory words resembling code addresses are candidates, not a proven unwind.
limitations: Stack coloration gives historical high-water usage; corruption can invalidate it.

families.title: Call stack and symbol hints
families.description: Frame-pointer or architecture-specific call-chain output.

source_refs.source_excerpt: int up_backtrace(struct tcb_s *tcb, void **buffer, int size, int skip)

recognition: symbol is not found in system map
analysis_guidance: Use the exact ELF/System.map and app text base to symbolize. Preserve unresolved frames.
Check whether output came from a true unwinder versus raw stack scanning.
limitations: Inlining, omitted frame pointers, optimized code and corrupted frames can truncate/untrust the chain.

families.title: Stack overflow / pressure
families.description: Explicit overflow notices and task stack summary.
analysis_guidance: Treat explicit overflow as evidence, high usage as a risk signal. Compare per-task used/total and MPU/stack-limit status.
limitations: A high-water mark alone cannot locate the overwriting instruction.

families.title: Task table and TCB
families.description: PID, priority, stack, TCB, state, lockcount and wait objects.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg_noarg("List of all tasks in the system\n");

recognition: List of all tasks in the system
analysis_guidance: Parse header-driven columns because NAME/USED columns depend on config.
Map numeric task states with the exact revision; correlate wait object addresses across tasks.
limitations: A single blocked task snapshot is not proof of deadlock.

families.title: Task scheduling history
families.description: Ring-buffer samples with time, optional task name, PID, priority and TCB.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("Displaying the TASK SCHEDULING HISTORY for %d count\n", max_task_count);

analysis_guidance: Respect ring order, finite capacity and timestamp units; identify missed wakeups/starvation only with corroborating time and state.
limitations: CONFIG not enabled / monitoring not enabled must be reported as unavailable evidence.

families.title: Interrupt scheduling history
families.description: IRQ time, number and ISR address plus interrupt counters.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("Displaying the IRQ SCHEDULING HISTORY for %d count\n", max_irq_count);

analysis_guidance: Relate IRQ frequency and last handlers to the fault timestamp and board vector table.
limitations: Counters need a time interval before claiming an interrupt storm.

families.title: Semaphore events and holders
families.description: Ring states IN/AQ/RL/WT/DR/UN, semaphore/TCB/PID, holder failures.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("Displaying the SEMAPHORE HISTORY for %d count\n", max_sem_count);
lldbg("IN:INIT AQ:AQUIRED RL:RELEASED WT:WAITING DR: DESTROY UN:UNKNOWN\n");

analysis_guidance: PID -1 means ISR and TCB field references ISR per the source legend.
Construct only observed wait/ownership edges; truncated history cannot prove a complete deadlock cycle.
limitations: AQ label is spelled AQUIRED in source; ordering/ownership can be incomplete after ring wrap.

families.title: Workqueue crash context
families.description: Assertion identifies currently executing work callback.
analysis_guidance: Symbolize the work callback and inspect its queue/lock dependencies; distinguish callback from worker thread entry.
limitations: No ordinary queue event trace is guaranteed by this assertion-only output.

families.title: Heap metadata corruption
families.description: Forward/backward traversal, guard nodes and corrupted-range dump.

source_refs.source_excerpt: mfdbg("ERROR: Heap corruption detected. Check below nodes for possible corruption.\n");

analysis_guidance: Do not classify the explicit negative No heap corruption detected as corruption.
Keep neighbors, sizes, owner allocation PC and dump boundaries; the detected node is not necessarily the writer.
limitations: The source config intentionally spells CORRPUTED; traversal diagnostics can be interrupted by further faults.

families.title: Double free / unallocated free
families.description: Free/alloc ownership PCs and PIDs when tracking enabled.

source_refs.source_excerpt: mdbg("WARNING!! Attempt for double freeing a pointer or releasing an unallocated pointer\n");
mdbg("1st free: released by %s (%d) at addr 0x%08x\n", task_name, node->free_call_pid, node->free_call_addr);
mdbg("2nd free (double free): now try to release by %s (%d) at addr 0x%08x\n", task_name, free_call_pid, free_call_addr);

analysis_guidance: Correlate allocator and both free callsites with thread lifetimes and ownership transfer.
limitations: A corrupted allocation flag may mimic a double free; preserve the source warning qualification.

families.title: OOM / fragmentation / alignment
families.description: Requested size, heap, caller, maximum contiguous block and total free size.

source_refs.source_excerpt: mfdbg("Allocation failed from %s heap.\n", (heap_type == KERNEL_HEAP) ? KERNEL_STR : USER_STR);
mfdbg(" - largest algined free size : %d\n", info.mxordblk);
mdbg("Allocation failed!!! We dont have enough memory. Try to free dead task stack areas\n");

analysis_guidance: Compare request including alignment/metadata against contiguous free size and correct heap.
Total free exceeding request with insufficient maximum block suggests fragmentation/alignment, not necessarily memory exhaustion.
limitations: GC may recover allocation after the warning; inspect subsequent return/retry evidence.

families.title: Heap usage, allocation ownership and fragmentation
families.description: Region nodes, total/current/peak/free, dead-thread allocation and bins.

source_refs.source_excerpt: heap_dbg("     Summary of Heap Usages (Size in Bytes)\n");
heap_dbg("(*)  Alive allocation by dead threads might be used by others or might be a leakage.\n");

analysis_guidance: Do not equate allocation owned by a dead thread with a confirmed leak; source allows ownership transfer.
Use repeated snapshots and allocation PCs to establish growth.
limitations: Heap dumps may be deliberately stopped to avoid watchdog expiry.

families.title: Procfs task / CPU / stack snapshots
families.description: Human-readable task status and stack metrics from procfs.
analysis_guidance: Record acquisition command/time; these are observations while reading, not an atomic global snapshot.
Interpret priority inheritance base/current pair only when available.
limitations: Most procfs output is assembled by snprintf, intentionally outside the direct-output inventory.

families.title: Task liveness monitor
families.description: Registration errors and reset path on missing heartbeat.
analysis_guidance: The missed-heartbeat reset path has no guaranteed unique log banner. Ask for monitor registration/status and reboot reason evidence.
limitations: Cannot identify monitor-induced reset merely from log silence or generic registration text.

families.title: Watchdog / reset / silent reboot
families.description: Watchdog driver control errors, silent reboot scheduling and reason recording.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg("Perform SILENT REBOOT expired by periodic timer!!\n");
dbg("Reboot watchdog will be expired after %d seconds\n", timeout);

analysis_guidance: Separate requested reset, reset cause saved in hardware, and successful post-reset boot.
Driver-control logs alone are not evidence that a hardware watchdog fired.
limitations: Reason register format and retention differ by board; missing logs cannot prove a reboot cause.

families.title: Binary-manager fault recovery
families.description: Fault notification, deactivation, reload request, failure/reset.

source_refs.source_excerpt: bmllvdbg("Try to recover fault with binid %d\n", bin_idx);
bmllvdbg("Loading thread with pid %d will reload binaries!\n", ret);

recognition: Try to recover fault with binid
analysis_guidance: Track binary ID and request through reload completion and resumed application activity.
A reload request is not proof of recovery.
limitations: ARMv8-M flat recipe cannot exercise every loadable recovery path.

families.title: Boot parameter / A-B slot validation
families.description: CRC, versions, active slot and kernel/app/resource set consistency.

source_refs.source_excerpt: bmdbg("BP set mismatch: kernel %u, app[%u:%s] %u\n", active_idx, bp_app_idx, bp_data->head.app_data[bp_app_idx].name, app_idx);
bmdbg("Set %s validation PASS, highest version %u\n", GET_PARTNAME(set_idx), highest_version);
bmdbg("Fail to crc check : %u != %u\n", calculate_crc, crc_hash);

analysis_guidance: Distinguish CRC/format validation from successful execution; associate app and resource slots with chosen kernel set.
limitations: Generic PASS/FAIL here are not kernel_tc results.

families.title: Loadable module addresses
families.description: Module entry/text/ro/data/stack/constructors for address attribution.
analysis_guidance: Use the exact app ELF and actual relocated section bases; kernel ELF alone cannot symbolize all app PCs.
limitations: Addresses can change after binary reload; identify the mapping valid at crash time.

families.title: Filesystem and storage errors
families.description: Mount/bind/block-driver/path diagnostics and negative errno.

source_refs.source_excerpt: fdbg("ERROR: Failed to find block driver %s\n", source);
fdbg("ERROR: PID %d is no longer valid\n", (int)pid);

analysis_guidance: Correlate filesystem, device, path, operation and errno; distinguish a disappearing procfs PID from storage corruption.
limitations: Filesystem-specific and board storage protocols need additional source and runtime coverage.

families.title: Network and driver diagnostic candidates
families.description: Network manager/socket/WLAN and peripheral output discovered by source inventory.
analysis_guidance: Emitter names here identify source routes, not guaranteed serial prefixes. Locate the matching literal and source subsystem through the inventory.
Correlate errno/status with connection and driver lifecycle; do not infer a kernel crash from an ordinary recoverable network error.
limitations: Generic discovery/manual AI review only; no claim of universal vendor-protocol decoding.
QEMU does not validate physical WLAN, DMA or peripheral timing.

families.title: Log transport, compression and truncation
families.description: Log dump failures, buffer/compression state and watchdog-limited capture.

source_refs.source_excerpt: ldplldbg("Compression failed for %d seconds, The device hang is suspected.\n", CONFIG_LOG_DUMP_HANG_CHECK_SEC);
mfdbg("It stops printing heap usage, to prevent watchdog reboot.\n");

analysis_guidance: Treat suspected hang as source heuristic, not proof. Preserve raw bytes and decode compressed/binary dumps using the matching format before text parsing.
Flag truncated/dropped output and do not fill missing register values.
limitations: Plain text parser does not decompress every board log-dump or binary crash format.

families.title: Debug level / prefix routing
families.description: Compile-time subsystem gates and logm/syslog/low-level output routes.

source_refs.source_excerpt: /* Temporary LOGM macros to route all dbg messages.

analysis_guidance: Capture .config and source revision; an unavailable gate means missing observability, not a healthy subsystem.
Retain original prefixes and line numbers while allowing ANSI/CR cleanup in normalized matching.
limitations: Local #undef/#define can override normal debug config; inventory conditions are not evaluated build eligibility.

families.title: Kernel test harness result
families.description: Explicit suite start/end counters and individual test assertions.

source_refs.source_excerpt: printf("\n########## %s End [PASS : %d, FAIL : %d] ##########\n", tc_name, total_pass, total_fail);

analysis_guidance: Require the complete intended suite footer and zero failures; separate expected negative test diagnostics from actual assertion crashes.
A timeout, incomplete suite or crash before footer remains incomplete even if some tests passed.
limitations: A passing QEMU suite proves only that tested image/config/emulator run, not hardware equivalence.

families.title: Memory leak checker results
families.description: LEAK/BROKEN allocation rows, totals, buffer limits and app text mappings.

source_refs.source_excerpt: printf("LEAK   | %10p |  %8d  | %10p | %d\n", (void *)((char *)node + SIZEOF_MM_ALLOCNODE), node->size - SIZEOF_MM_ALLOCNODE, owner_addr, pid);
printf("Available buffer size (%d) is small.\nPlease increase CONFIG_MEM_LEAK_CHECKER_MAX_ALLOC_COUNT value more than %d.\n", MAX_ALLOC_COUNT, node_cnt);

analysis_guidance: Preserve explicit negative NO MEMORY LEAK and partial/failed scanner state.
Map owner PC to kernel/app/common binary using captured text ranges; a LEAK row is a checker finding that needs lifetime/ownership investigation.
limitations: Pointer-reachability scanning has coverage and allocation-count limits; do not equate zero findings with proof of no lifetime leaks.

families.title: Periodic live/terminated thread stack monitor
families.description: PID, active/inactive status, stack size, peak stack/heap and time.
analysis_guidance: Use header-dependent columns and separate inactive thread historical records from current task state.
Compare repeated per-task peaks against allocation size; preserve timestamp units.
limitations: A high-water snapshot does not identify exact stack frames at the peak.

families.title: MPU region and permission table
families.description: Region base/size/enabled state, privileged/user access and execute-never.

source_refs.source_excerpt: lldbg_noarg("List of MPU regions and permissions\n");

recognition: List of MPU regions and permissions
analysis_guidance: Match fault address and instruction PC to enabled region bounds, privilege mode and X/XN permission.
Keep v8-M base/limit semantics separate from v7-M size/subregion attributes.
limitations: Disabled region rows can show meaningless derived size; do not treat them as active memory regions.

families.title: Procfs error-report marker
families.description: Task identity retained in the error-report procfs surface.

source_refs.source_excerpt: linesize = snprintf(efile->line, EREPORT_LINELEN, "Error_Report pid:%d, taskaddr:%lu", pid, taskaddr);

analysis_guidance: Treat this as an identity/context marker and request accompanying fault registers, assertion and payload.
limitations: Marker alone does not explain cause; task address is printed decimal by this emitter.
